notes: Human-authored synthetic enterprise support cases derived from public troubleshooting and KCS failure patterns. No customer records or vendor article text are copied. This is a realistic development seed, not a production-quality benchmark.

knowledge_documents.title: Troubleshoot device-compliance Conditional Access blocks
knowledge_documents.text:
# Device compliance access troubleshooting

When a user is blocked because a device is not compliant, confirm the device is enrolled, identify the failing compliance setting, remediate it, then run a fresh device access/compliance check. Allow the updated compliance state to register before retrying the protected application. A device-compliance error is different from a domain-join or approved-app error.

knowledge_documents.title: Approved application Conditional Access failures
knowledge_documents.text:
# Approved application access

If a sign-in is blocked because the application is not approved, verify the Conditional Access error and retry with an application that satisfies the approved-app policy. Do not treat an approved-app failure as a device-compliance failure.

knowledge_documents.title: Enrollment blocked by device limit
knowledge_documents.text:
# Device enrollment limit

When enrollment fails because a user has reached the permitted device count, compare the configured enrollment limit with the user's enrolled devices. Remove obsolete device records or change the approved limit before retrying enrollment.

knowledge_documents.title: Company Portal unavailable or corrupted
knowledge_documents.text:
# Company Portal repair

For a Company Portal unavailable error, confirm the user can sign in through the management web portal and test another network. If web sign-in succeeds, update or reinstall Company Portal and retry enrollment. If the symptom persists, continue diagnosis instead of repeatedly reinstalling the app.

knowledge_documents.title: Baseline Intune enrollment checks
knowledge_documents.text:
# Enrollment baseline checks

Confirm that the user has the required license, the device is eligible for enrollment, management authority is configured, and the user can authenticate to the enrollment service. Capture the exact enrollment error before changing policy.

knowledge_documents.title: Cloud IAM policy evaluation checklist
knowledge_documents.text:
# IAM policy evaluation

When an identity policy appears to allow an action but the request is denied, inspect all policy layers that contribute to effective permissions. Identity policies are only one layer; organization controls, resource policies, boundaries, and service-specific controls can further restrict access.

knowledge_documents.title: Explicit deny overrides an allow
knowledge_documents.text:
# Explicit deny handling

An explicit deny in an applicable policy overrides an allow. For an unexpected access-denied result, identify the principal, resource, action, and all applicable organization, identity, and resource policies. Remove or narrow a deny only through the approved change process.

knowledge_documents.title: Role assumption and trust-policy troubleshooting
knowledge_documents.text:
# Role trust troubleshooting

If a principal cannot assume a role, verify the role trust relationship, caller permission to assume the role, external-ID or condition requirements, and the principal identity used by the workload.

knowledge_documents.title: Cloud endpoint policy and network access
knowledge_documents.text:
# Endpoint access controls

Requests routed through a private service endpoint can be restricted by the endpoint policy in addition to identity permissions. Confirm the network path and endpoint policy when access differs between network locations.

knowledge_documents.title: Customer portal request requires a valid request type
knowledge_documents.text:
# Request type and portal visibility

A service request must have a valid customer request type to open correctly in the customer portal. Requests created from generic issue-creation paths or moved between projects can lose that mapping. Set a request type compatible with the issue type and verify the customer portal link.

knowledge_documents.title: Customer portal access checklist
knowledge_documents.text:
# Customer portal access

For a customer who cannot view a request, confirm the request has a valid request type, the customer can access the service project, and the customer is the reporter, a request participant, or a member of an organization with which the request is shared.

knowledge_documents.title: Reporter visibility and portal request lists
knowledge_documents.text:
# Reporter field and request lists

Customer request lists depend on the reporter relationship. If the reporter field is hidden by configuration, portal request lists can fail to show the expected requests. Restore the reporter field and re-test the customer view.

knowledge_documents.title: Customer notification troubleshooting
knowledge_documents.text:
# Customer notifications

If a customer can open a request but does not receive notifications, verify notification rules, customer notification settings, the request participant/reporting relationship, and email delivery status.

knowledge_documents.title: Emergency access account credential rotation
knowledge_documents.text:
# Emergency account credential rotation

Rotate emergency access credentials through the privileged identity process, verify monitored sign-in capability, and store recovery material according to the security runbook.

knowledge_documents.title: Organization policy administrator runbook
knowledge_documents.text:
# Organization policy administration

Changes to organization-wide deny controls require cloud governance approval, an impact review, and a rollback plan. Validate the target scope before applying a deny to production.

knowledge_documents.title: Service-management automation administration
knowledge_documents.text:
# Automation administration

Changes to service-project automation rules require an administrator role. Validate trigger scope, conditions, and audit-log execution before enabling a rule for all projects.

knowledge_documents.title: Corporate VPN certificate renewal
knowledge_documents.text:
# VPN certificate renewal

If VPN authentication fails because the device certificate is expired, renew the managed certificate and verify the new certificate is presented by the VPN client before reconnecting.

knowledge_documents.title: Purchase-order approval routing
knowledge_documents.text:
# Purchase-order routing

Purchase orders above the configured threshold require finance approval before release. Routing problems should be checked against the approval matrix and cost-center ownership.

case_record.short_description: SharePoint blocked with AADSTS53000 after BitLocker remediation
case_record.description: A managed Windows 11 laptop was denied access to SharePoint with AADSTS53000. The user had enabled BitLocker after Company Portal reported encryption as the only failed compliance setting.
comments: User confirmed browser sign-in worked until the compliance policy began enforcing encryption.

work_notes.text: Intune showed the device as noncompliant because encryption was not detected.
BitLocker was enabled and encryption completed, but SharePoint still returned AADSTS53000.
Ran Check access in Company Portal. The compliance state changed to compliant after synchronization; the next SharePoint sign-in succeeded.

case_record.resolution_notes: Confirmed the device was enrolled, remediated the failed encryption control, forced a fresh compliance/access check, and validated successful SharePoint access after the compliant state registered.

retrieval_queries.query: AADSTS53000 device noncompliant after BitLocker enabled
Company Portal says encryption fixed but SharePoint still blocks the laptop

case_record.short_description: Teams desktop remains blocked after device is compliant
case_record.description: A Windows laptop had become compliant and Microsoft 365 web access worked, but Teams desktop continued to fail with AADSTS53000 using an older session.
comments: User could open the protected service in a browser after the compliance check.

work_notes.text: Confirmed Company Portal reported the device compliant and browser access succeeded.
Teams desktop was still using an earlier sign-in session created before compliance was refreshed.
Signed out of the desktop client, closed it, reopened it, and completed a fresh modern-authentication sign-in. Access succeeded.

case_record.resolution_notes: After confirming current device compliance and successful browser access, forced a fresh desktop-client sign-in so the application evaluated the current device state. Teams access then succeeded.

article_expectation.subject: Desktop application remains blocked after device becomes compliant

evidence.text:
# Device compliance access troubleshooting

When a user is blocked because a device is not compliant, confirm the device is enrolled, identify the failing compliance setting, remediate it, then run a fresh device access/compliance check. Allow the updated compliance state to register before retrying the protected application. A device-compliance error is different from a domain-join or approved-app error.

The device was compliant and browser access succeeded. The desktop client was signed out and restarted so a fresh modern-authentication sign-in evaluated the current device state; access then succeeded.

reference_article.title: Desktop application remains blocked after device compliance is restored

issue_description.text: A desktop application can continue to reject access even after the device has returned to a compliant state.

symptoms.text: Company Portal reports the device as compliant.
Browser access succeeds while the desktop client still fails.

diagnostic_checks.text: Confirm the device currently reports compliant and test the protected service in a browser.

resolution_steps.text: After compliance is confirmed, sign out of the affected desktop client, close it, reopen it, and complete a fresh sign-in.

expected_result.text: The desktop application evaluates the current device state and access succeeds.

exceptions.text: If browser access is also blocked, continue the base device-compliance remediation path first.

case_record.short_description: New Conditional Access policy blocked administrator access
case_record.description: A policy requiring compliant devices was enabled for all administrators and all cloud resources. Two administrators on unmanaged recovery workstations received AADSTS53003 and could no longer enter the admin portals.
comments: A monitored emergency account retained access because it had been excluded by a separate emergency-access control.

work_notes.text: Sign-in diagnostics showed the newly enabled device-compliance policy as the blocking control.
Used the emergency account to place the policy back into a non-enforcing state and add the approved emergency-access exclusions.
Re-enabled the policy for a pilot admin group, validated sign-ins, then expanded scope after review.

case_record.resolution_notes: Recovered administrator access through the monitored emergency account, corrected emergency-access exclusions, and changed the rollout from all-admin enforcement to a validated pilot before broader scope.

retrieval_queries.query: conditional access policy locked administrators out after requiring compliant devices
AADSTS53003 admins cannot open Entra portal after all-user policy rollout
safe rollout and emergency account exclusions for device compliance policy

article_expectation.subject: Roll out a device-compliance Conditional Access policy without locking out administrators

evidence.text: Sign-in diagnostics identified the newly enabled device-compliance policy as the blocking control for administrator sign-ins.
Recovery used a monitored emergency account; the policy was returned to a non-enforcing state and approved emergency-access exclusions were added.
The policy was re-enabled for a pilot administrator group, sign-ins were validated, and scope was expanded only after review.

reference_article.title: Roll out device-compliance Conditional Access safely for administrators

purpose.text: Apply a device-compliance access policy without losing administrative recovery access.

prerequisites.text: A monitored emergency-access path must be available before enforcing the policy broadly.

steps.text: Validate which Conditional Access policy would block the administrator sign-in.
Keep approved emergency-access accounts outside the blocking scope.
Enable enforcement for a pilot administrator group and validate sign-ins.
Expand scope only after the pilot behavior has been reviewed.

expected_result.text: Administrator access is protected by the new control while the approved emergency path remains available.

case_record.short_description: Company Portal temporarily unavailable during enrollment
case_record.description: Company Portal displayed a temporary-unavailable message. Reinstalling the app did not change the error, while web sign-in worked normally.
comments: The same user had recently enrolled several test devices.

work_notes.text: Web sign-in succeeded, so credentials and basic service reachability were not the immediate failure.
Reinstalling Company Portal did not change the symptom.
The user was at the configured device limit. After one verified stale test device was removed, enrollment completed.

case_record.resolution_notes: Used web sign-in to rule out an authentication outage, then checked the enrollment count after app repair did not help. Removing a stale device brought the user below the limit and enrollment completed.

article_expectation.subject: Company Portal reports temporary unavailability during enrollment

evidence.text:
# Company Portal repair

For a Company Portal unavailable error, confirm the user can sign in through the management web portal and test another network. If web sign-in succeeds, update or reinstall Company Portal and retry enrollment. If the symptom persists, continue diagnosis instead of repeatedly reinstalling the app.

# Device enrollment limit

When enrollment fails because a user has reached the permitted device count, compare the configured enrollment limit with the user's enrolled devices. Remove obsolete device records or change the approved limit before retrying enrollment.
Web sign-in worked and reinstalling Company Portal did not help. The enrolled-device count was at the configured limit; removing a verified stale device allowed enrollment to complete.

reference_article.title: Company Portal temporarily unavailable during enrollment

issue_description.text: Enrollment can present the same temporary-unavailable symptom for both application problems and device-limit problems.

symptoms.text: Company Portal reports temporary unavailability while enrollment cannot complete.

diagnostic_checks.text: Confirm whether the user can sign in through the management web portal.
If app repair does not resolve the problem, compare the user's enrolled-device count with the configured limit.

resolution_steps.text: Repair or reinstall Company Portal when the application is the failing component.
When the device limit is reached, remove only verified obsolete records or follow the approved limit-change process.

expected_result.text: Enrollment completes after the actual failing condition is corrected.

case_record.short_description: S3 PutObject denied although role policy allows it
case_record.description: A deployment role had an identity policy allowing PutObject to the release bucket, but uploads returned AccessDenied after an organization-policy change.
comments: The failure started immediately after an organization control was tightened.

work_notes.text: Confirmed the role identity policy allowed PutObject to the expected bucket path.
An organization-level service control policy contained an explicit deny matching the release account.
Narrowed the deny through the approved change process and re-ran the deployment upload successfully.

case_record.resolution_notes: The identity allow was overridden by an organization-level explicit deny. The deny scope was corrected through approved change control and the PutObject operation then succeeded.

retrieval_queries.query: S3 PutObject AccessDenied even though IAM role has allow policy

case_record.short_description: DynamoDB update denied after adding allow to application role
case_record.description: An application role was granted dynamodb:UpdateItem in its identity policy, but the operation remained denied.
comments: Read operations on the same table continued to work.

work_notes.text: Verified the identity policy allowed UpdateItem on the target table.
The role had a permissions boundary that allowed read actions but did not allow UpdateItem.
Updated the approved boundary policy to include the required write action and validated the application update.

case_record.resolution_notes: The permissions boundary capped the role's effective permissions below the identity policy. After the approved boundary was updated to allow UpdateItem, the application write succeeded.

retrieval_queries.query: DynamoDB UpdateItem denied although role identity policy allows it permissions boundary
role can read DynamoDB but cannot write after adding allow policy
effective permissions limited by boundary despite IAM allow

article_expectation.subject: Why can an AWS role remain denied after an allow is added?

evidence.text:
# IAM policy evaluation

When an identity policy appears to allow an action but the request is denied, inspect all policy layers that contribute to effective permissions. Identity policies are only one layer; organization controls, resource policies, boundaries, and service-specific controls can further restrict access.
The role identity policy allowed UpdateItem, but a permissions boundary allowed only read actions. Updating the approved boundary to include UpdateItem made the write succeed.

reference_article.title: Why can an AWS role remain denied after an allow is added?

introduction.text: Effective permissions are determined across multiple policy layers, so an identity-policy allow does not by itself guarantee access.

items.question: What should I check when the identity policy already allows the action?

answer.text: Inspect the other policy layers that constrain effective permissions, including a permissions boundary when one is attached to the role.

items.question: What happened in the example case?

answer.text: The role's permissions boundary allowed reads but not DynamoDB UpdateItem; after the approved boundary was extended, the write succeeded.

case_record.short_description: Application can read S3 object but cannot decrypt it with KMS
case_record.description: A workload successfully retrieved an encrypted object from S3 but failed with KMS AccessDenied during decryption after a key was replaced.
comments: The role already had kms:Decrypt in an IAM policy.

work_notes.text: S3 GetObject succeeded, isolating the failure to the encryption/decryption path.
The replacement KMS key policy did not include the application role used by the workload.
Added the role through the approved key-policy change, then validated decryption from the application.

case_record.resolution_notes: The replacement KMS key policy omitted the application role. After the approved key policy granted the role access, the same object could be retrieved and decrypted successfully.

retrieval_queries.query: S3 GetObject works but KMS decrypt AccessDenied on encrypted object
role has kms Decrypt IAM permission but key policy omits role
new KMS key causes application decryption failure while S3 access succeeds

article_expectation.subject: S3 object retrieval succeeds but KMS decryption is denied

evidence.text: S3 GetObject succeeded, isolating the problem to the encryption/decryption path.
The replacement KMS key policy did not include the application role used by the workload.
After an approved key-policy change added the role, application decryption succeeded.

reference_article.title: S3 object retrieval succeeds but KMS decryption is denied

issue_description.text: A workload can have permission to retrieve an encrypted S3 object while separately lacking authorization to decrypt it with the KMS key.

symptoms.text: S3 GetObject succeeds but the application receives KMS AccessDenied during decryption.

diagnostic_checks.text: Confirm that object retrieval succeeds so storage access can be separated from the decryption failure.
Inspect whether the active KMS key policy includes the workload role.

resolution_steps.text: Apply the approved key-policy change that grants the workload role the required access.

expected_result.text: The application can retrieve and decrypt the same encrypted object.

case_record.resolution_notes: The agent-created issue had no customer request type. A compatible request type was assigned and the customer verified that the request became visible in the portal.

case_record.short_description: Reporter cannot see request even though request type and portal access are valid
case_record.description: A customer had portal access and the request had a valid request type, but the request was absent from My Requests while agents could open it.
comments: The customer was the reporter and could open other requests in the same service project.

work_notes.text: Verified request type, portal access, and reporter relationship were correct.
The issue security level on this request did not include the reporter/portal-customer role.
Updated the security-level membership and verified the reporter could see the request.

case_record.resolution_notes: The portal prerequisites were valid, but the issue security level excluded the customer. Updating the security level to include the reporter/portal-customer role restored request visibility.

article_expectation.subject: Customer cannot see a JSM request after basic portal checks pass

evidence.text:
# Customer portal access

For a customer who cannot view a request, confirm the request has a valid request type, the customer can access the service project, and the customer is the reporter, a request participant, or a member of an organization with which the request is shared.
Request type, portal access, and reporter relationship were valid. The issue security level excluded the reporter/portal-customer role; adding that role restored visibility.

reference_article.title: Customer cannot see a JSM request after the basic portal checks pass

issue_description.text: A request can remain hidden even when request type, portal access, and reporter relationship are correct if issue security excludes the customer.

symptoms.text: Agents can open the request but the reporter cannot see it in the portal.

diagnostic_checks.text: Confirm the request type, customer portal access, and reporter/participant relationship first.
If those checks pass, inspect the issue security level for the reporter or portal-customer role.

resolution_steps.text: Update the applicable security-level membership through the normal administration process so the reporter/portal-customer role is included.

expected_result.text: The reporter can see the request in the customer portal.

case_record.short_description: JSM email channel stopped creating requests after request-type change
case_record.description: Incoming support email stopped creating service requests after the default email request type was changed to require a custom field that email messages could not populate.
comments: Portal-created requests using the same issue type still worked.

work_notes.text: Email-channel diagnostics reported that no suitable request type was available.
The configured default request type required a custom business-impact field in addition to summary and description.
Created an email-compatible request type with summary and description visible and all additional fields optional, then validated a new inbound email.

case_record.resolution_notes: The email channel's default request type required a field that email could not populate. An email-compatible request type was configured and inbound email request creation succeeded.

reference_article.title: Configure a request type for the JSM email channel

purpose.text: Configure a request type that incoming email can populate without requiring fields that are unavailable from email content.

prerequisites.text: Email-channel diagnostics indicate that no suitable request type is available.

steps.text: Use a request type where Summary and Description are visible.
Keep additional visible fields optional when inbound email cannot supply them.
Assign the compatible request type to the email channel and test with a new inbound message.

expected_result.text: A new inbound email creates a service request successfully.
